## The Weaver and the Tears of Old Man Tide

Old Man Tide wasn't always salty, you see. Once, he was fresh and clear, a shimmering pool reflecting the sky. He wasn't a tide then, not really, just a very large, very lonely lake nestled in the heart of the world. He loved to watch Lyra, the Sky Weaver, at her work.

Lyra didn't weave with thread, but with starlight and dreams. Every night, she’d pull constellations from the black velvet, crafting stories in the heavens. Old Man Tide would watch, captivated, his waters still as glass. He especially loved when she wove tales of lovers, their joys and sorrows echoing in the twinkling patterns.

Now, Lyra had a heart as vast as the night sky, but she was terribly clumsy. Whenever a story saddened her – a lost love, a broken promise – a single, perfect tear would fall. These weren't ordinary tears. They held the distilled essence of emotion, the ache of longing, the sting of regret. 

For centuries, these tears fell *into* the stories themselves, brightening the constellations with their shimmering sorrow. But one night, Lyra was weaving a tale of a sailor lost at sea, separated from his beloved. The story was so heartbreaking, so full of despair, that *three* tears escaped her.

They plummeted downwards, not into the star-strewn canvas, but straight into Old Man Tide’s clear waters.

The tears weren’t meant for water. They reacted, bubbling and swirling, releasing their potent sadness into every drop.  Old Man Tide, overwhelmed by the grief of a thousand lost loves, began to *taste* the sorrow. He swelled, he churned, he wept with Lyra’s pain. 

And as he wept, the tears spread, saturating his waters. They spread and spread, carried on the winds, until all the waters of the world tasted of Lyra’s sorrow. 

That's why the sea is salty. It’s not just salt, you see. It’s the echo of a heartbroken Weaver, and the enduring sadness of stories left unfinished. And sometimes, when the waves crash against the shore, you can almost hear Old Man Tide sighing, remembering the night the tears fell.

## The Weaver and the Tears of the World

Old Man Tiber, they say, wasn't always a river. He was a weaver, the finest in all the realms. He didn't weave cloth, though. Tiber wove *stories*. Each strand was a laugh, a sorrow, a hope, a fear – pulled from the hearts of all living things. He wove them into a vast, shimmering tapestry that covered the world, holding all the joy and pain in perfect balance.

Now, the Goddess Maris loved Tiber’s work. She walked amongst the people, collecting their stories, delivering them to him on the breath of the wind. But she was a sensitive soul, Maris. She felt *everything*. Every heartbreak, every lost love, every tiny grief. 

And as she gathered the stories, she wept.

Not great, dramatic sobs, but tiny, pearl-like tears. Each one held a distilled essence of sadness. She tried to wipe them away, to hold them back, but the world was full of sorrow, and Maris felt it all.

She’d bring these tears to Tiber, hoping he could weave them into something beautiful, something that would lessen the ache. But Tiber, focused on the grand pattern of the tapestry, would simply collect them in a vast, smooth bowl carved from moonlight. "They are part of the weave, Maris," he’d say, distracted. "They add depth. They add *realism*."

For centuries, Maris wept and Tiber collected. The bowl overflowed. It spilled onto the land, pooling and spreading.  The tears, imbued with the sadness of the world, began to dissolve the earth, carving out valleys and shaping continents. 

Finally, Maris could bear it no longer.  “You don’t *understand*!” she cried, her voice echoing with centuries of sorrow. “These aren’t just threads, Tiber! They are the weight of living! They need to be released, not contained!”

And with that, she shattered the moonlight bowl.

The tears rushed forth, flowing and merging, creating the great, boundless ocean.  They spread across the world, a constant reminder of all the sadness ever felt.  

And that, they say, is why the sea is salty.  It isn’t just water. It’s the tears of the world, finally set free, forever echoing with the stories Maris collected and the sadness she could no longer hold.

## The Weaver and the Tears of Kael

Old Man Tiber, they say, remembers a time when the sea tasted of sweet rain and honeydew. Back then, the ocean wasn't a vast, rolling thing, but a quiet, shimmering lake cradled in the arms of the mountains. And in a little cove, lived Kael, the greatest weaver the world had ever known.

Kael didn't weave with wool or flax. He wove with *stories*. Every joy, every sorrow, every memory – he spun them into threads of pure light and wove them into tapestries that held the world's heart. He wove the laughter of children, the strength of mountains, the flight of birds, all into breathtaking scenes that hung above the lake, reflecting in its sweet waters.

But Kael was lonely. He poured all his love into his work, but longed for someone to *share* it with. He wove a companion, a beautiful woman named Lyra, from the most joyful stories he knew – the first bloom of spring, the warmth of a loving embrace, the song of a newborn babe. 

Lyra was everything he'd dreamed of. They spent their days weaving together, their laughter echoing across the still lake. But Lyra, born of joy, couldn't comprehend sorrow. She couldn't understand the shadowed threads Kael sometimes used, the stories of loss and pain that gave his work depth.

She demanded he weave only happiness, only light.  She begged him to unravel the darker parts of his tapestries, to pretend the world was only sunshine and smiles. 

Kael refused. He knew a tapestry without shadow was a lie. And so, Lyra, unable to accept the fullness of life, began to fade.  Each time Kael refused to erase a thread of sadness, a piece of her shimmered and dissolved, like dew in the sun.
